subject: Cognitive Science
title: Goal-Derived Categories
description: A short lesson to help you apply Goal-Derived Categories.

hook.text: "Things to grab if the house is on fire." That's a real category, but no textbook lists it.

buildup.text: Ad hoc categories are created on the fly to serve a goal, not stored in long-term memory.

discovery.text: Lawrence Barsalou showed that these categories have graded structure just like natural ones.

twist.text: Passport is more typical of "things to save in a fire" than piano. Typicality tracks usefulness.

climax.text: This proves categorization is flexible—the mind builds new groups whenever goals demand it.

punchline.text: Need invents categories on the spot.

details.summary: Not all categories are based on similarity. Goal-derived categories like things to grab in a fire or foods to eat on a diet group dissimilar items by shared purpose. These categories are created on the fly to serve immediate goals and reveal the flexibility of human categorization.
details.whyItMatters: Goal-derived categories show that human categorization is not limited to what looks alike. People create new categories dynamically as needs arise.
takeaways: Goal-derived categories group items by purpose, not similarity
They are constructed flexibly based on current needs
They reveal categorization as dynamic and context-dependent

faq.question: Who proposed the idea of goal-derived categories?
faq.answer: Lawrence Barsalou described them in the 1980s, showing that people can construct coherent categories like things to sell at a garage sale from items with no resemblance to each other. These categories have graded structure just like similarity-based ones, with better and worse members.

faq.question: Do goal-derived categories have prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Members that best serve the goal are rated as the most typical. In the category foods to eat on a diet, celery is a better member than pizza. The typicality gradient is determined by goal relevance rather than perceptual similarity, but the graded structure is the same.
